text:
- chief complaint: the patient presented to the emergency department after a fall with chest pain, ankle swelling, and shortness of breath, found to have congestive heart failure in the setting of uncontrolled hypertension.
- history of present illness: the patient has hypertension with a reported blood pressure of 200/90, often missed medications, and a high-sodium diet (frequent chips and fast food). Echocardiogram showed preserved ejection fraction (55%), normal diastolic filling, and mild to moderate mitral regurgitation. The patient had been smoking but reports cutting down to about one cigarette per week.
- physical examination: blood pressure 128/72 in clinic; no jugular venous distention; stable 2/6 systolic ejection murmur; clear lungs bilaterally; trace lower extremity edema.
- symptoms experienced by the patient: shortness of breath with exertion, ankle swelling, intermittent chest pain (attributed to heartburn), and fatigue on walking.
- new medications prescribed or changed, including dosages: bumetanide (Bumex) 2 mg once daily; losartan (Cozaar) 100 mg once daily; amlodipine (Norvasc) 5 mg once daily. All were continued, with emphasis on consistent adherence.
- follow-up instructions: daily weights, call the doctor for a gain of 3 pounds in 2 days; obtain a home blood pressure cuff and monitor BP at home; nutrition consult for a low-sodium diet; renal artery ultrasound ordered.
